question: In triangle ABC , AB = 6 cm, BC = 9 cm and AC = 12 cm. If AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC , where D is a point on BC then DC is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio of the base segments equals the ratio of the adjacent sides.

⇒ BD : DC = AB : AC

⇒ BD : DC = 6 : 12 = 1 : 2

⇒ DC corresponds to 2 parts out of the 3 total parts of BC.

⇒ DC = (2 ÷ 3) × 9 = 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In triangle ABC, AB = 6 cm, AC = 12 cm, and BC = 9 cm.

⇒ AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ The Internal Angle Bisector Theorem states that an angle bisector of a triangle divides the opposite side into two segments proportional to the other two sides.

⇒ AB ÷ AC = BD ÷ DC

**Calculation:**

⇒ 6 ÷ 12 = BD ÷ DC

⇒ BD ÷ DC = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ The segments BD and DC are in the ratio 1 : 2.

⇒ We know that BC = BD + DC = 9 cm.

⇒ Total ratio parts of BC = 1 + 2 = 3 parts.

⇒ 3 parts = 9 cm

⇒ 1 part = 3 cm

⇒ Since DC corresponds to 2 parts:

⇒ DC = 2 × 3 cm = 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

External Angle Bisector Theorem

If the external angle bisector of an angle intersects the opposite side extended, it divides the opposite side externally in the ratio of the other two sides. Formula: AB ÷ AC = BD ÷ CD.

Incenter of a Triangle

The point of intersection of all three internal angle bisectors is called the incenter. It is equidistant from all three sides, and the perpendicular distance to the sides is the inradius (r = Area ÷ Semi-perimeter).

Length of Angle Bisector

The length of the internal angle bisector AD can be found using the sides of the triangle and the base segments. Formula: AD² = (AB × AC) − (BD × DC).
